methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Standard Subsea is a seed-stage frontier-tech company in the Ocean & Maritime sector founded by Christopher Amidon. The company has raised $10M+ to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers (Clippership, NetworkOcean, Albacore) and no listed public companies, reflecting the nascent state of the subsector.

The valuation analysis applies one applicable method: Stage-Progression, which uses the $10M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement. This methodology yields a point estimate of $25M. The 2.5x step-up reflects expected value accretion as Standard Subsea progresses from seed through product-market validation and early traction milestones.

The triangulated range is $21M (low) to $29M (high), centered on a $25M median. Given the reliance on a single applicable method and a private-only comparables set with limited public reference points, this range carries meaningful estimation risk. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Standard Subsea's technology differentiation and market traction match peer trajectories, capital efficiency relative to the three private comparables, and the timing and terms of future funding events. The absence of public comps limits anchoring to market-derived multiples and increases reliance on stage-based progression assumptions.
